This week, Apple launched its next-generation M6 chip in the new Mac mini, but several other products are also set to upgrade to the M6 soon. Below is the rumored timeline for M6 Mac and iPad releases.

Fall 2026: MacBook Pro and iMac

Expected this fall (around October), Apple will release two more Macs equipped with the M6:

  • MacBook Pro
  • iMac

The MacBook Pro will only have a 14-inch base model. According to Mark Gurman, Apple is skipping the M6 Pro and Max versions, so only the entry-level MacBook Pro will upgrade to the M6. The next batch of Pro-tier chips won't arrive until the M7 Pro and M7 Max in 2027.

Apple's all-new iMac is not expected to change much beyond the M6 chip, with the only other rumored upgrade being the addition of a few new color options. However, going from M4 to M6, the new model is still worth upgrading to.

Worth noting is that the rumored MacBook Ultra is not on this list. It is expected to launch in the fall, but will use the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, not the M6.

Spring 2027: iPad Pro and MacBook Air

The first products rumored to upgrade to the M6 in 2027 include:

  • iPad Pro
  • MacBook Air

Apple last updated the iPad Pro in fall 2025, when it upgraded to the M5 chip. With the rumored spring 2027 update, the product will follow its usual 18-month upgrade cycle.

Beyond upgrading to the M6 chip, Apple's new iPad Pro is expected to feature a vapor chamber cooling design, which can improve the sustained performance of this ultra-thin machine.

The MacBook Air equipped with the M6 chip is expected to launch at the same time as the iPad Pro. February through April are all possible, but based on Apple's historical record, March is the safest bet.

Beyond the chip upgrade, there aren't many other rumors about the new MacBook Air. It should retain the same design as the M5 model, and reports indicate that the OLED upgrade won't appear until 2028 at the earliest, so the screen will most likely remain unchanged.

One potential benefit of the M6 for the iPad Pro and MacBook Air is longer battery life. Apple says the 2-nanometer process used in the M6 brings "a major leap in performance and energy efficiency."

Are you planning to upgrade to any of these new M6 products? Why? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
